card.title: Don’t Let Reality Notice
card.instruction: Behave as though openly questioning the impossible premise could attract dangerous attention, and respond to doubt with urgent normality.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lower your voice about the singing moon. We don't want it noticing us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then call it weather. Weather gets away with anything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's singing my name. Should I answer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only with 'Lovely evening.' Keep walking. We're just two people discussing the forecast.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's direct attention to narrow the response further and preserve ordinary conversation as cover.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a singing moon and explicit concern about being noticed.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's lovely-evening answer is earned by B4's reply question and A3's weather disguise.
